actions.name: list
actions.description: Discover active tables (data collections) for the user's product. When the user names or partially names a table, pass `query` to search table names instead of loading every table. Results are paginated: totalCount is the full match count, returnedCount is only this page, and nextPage requests the next page. Set `includeTrash: true` when the user asks to see deleted/trashed Sheets; the response includes a separate `trash` list with the exact deletionOperationId, tableName, restore deadlines, and databaseId needed by table_manage action "restore". Do NOT call this again once the table id is known: use table_query action "get" to read one known table's schema, fields, or views without repeating the table list.

actions.name: import_file
actions.description:
Upload an original CSV or Excel .xlsx file up to 25 MB into a new Sheet in the current Project. First use action prepare with a stable uploadId, exact filename, byteCount and description. Transfer the exact file bytes to the returned signed HTTP upload URL; never put base64, rows, paths or arbitrary download URLs in tool input. Then action start queues durable background processing. Poll action status with the same uploadId for processedRows, totalRows, imported and failedRows. Queued or processing is not success. For select_worksheet, ask the user to choose one returned worksheet, then action start with its exact name. Each import supports 5,000 data rows and 200 columns, infers typed fields, and leaves Enrich off. Completed results include the saved databaseId and actual fieldKeys. Retry unknown writes with the original operationId, uploadId and exact input; never prepare a replacement file to force a retry. If attachment bytes are inaccessible in the host, report that limitation.

actions.name: create
actions.description:
Create a new table (data collection) in the current Project — rows of signals, posts, events, or scratch data. Native Project Runs resolve scope from their Thread; external member calls carry their selected work Project in top-level projectId, outside this action input. Resolve and load the appropriate Project context before creating; a direct external member operation requires no Thread. For a permanent CRM entity whose rows are deduplicated, mergeable Records, use object_manage action "create" on the object capability instead; the Company and People templates here are ordinary Sheets that share those names. Call `table_templates action "search"` to choose Company, People, Creator, or Posts, then create with `template: <id>` — the server applies that template's schema and views. Any `schema.fields` are opt-in additions on top of the baseline. Custom fields and Company, Creator, and Posts fields start with Enrich off. People is the intentional outbound exception: its managed Work Email, Phone, and LinkedIn fields ship enabled with server-owned recipes and field-specific instructions. After creation, use `enrichment_manage action "enable"` only for other fields the user explicitly selected. When none fits, omit `template` and provide a full custom `schema`. Never call table_manage action "create" without either a template or a full schema; that input fails validation. For a typed Workflow package, wait for `workflow_templates action "get"` and pass its returned `createTableSchema` as this tool's `schema` instead of inventing or translating a schema in parallel. Every custom display pointer (`primary_field`, `subtitle_field`, `link_field`, `image_field`, `time_field`) must exactly name a key present in that same `schema.fields` array; omit an unsupported pointer rather than copying one from another table type. For an explicitly requested research Sheet, use `template: 'company'` for company research; CRM/TAM mapping should reuse Company Records and Lists through native discovery instead; use `template: 'creator'` for creator or influencer platform accounts. Growth-only Company fields such as tech_stack, fit_score, and fit_reason must be added explicitly only when the user selects those steps. A `description` (or `purpose`) is always required.

The result includes `fieldKeys`, `primaryField`, and `uniqueField`. Use those exact keys for later item_manage action "create" calls; never guess aliases.

Rules:
- Requires a Project context: pass projectId.
- Description or purpose is required.
- Sheet creation requires a template (find one with table_templates action "search") or a full custom schema.
- Blank table creation requires a full schema.

purpose.description: The user's goal / what this table is for, in their own words. Used as the table description when `description` is omitted.

reuseExisting.description: Set true only after the user explicitly chose to reuse the same-name existing table. Omit when creating a new table or when the user has not confirmed reuse.

template.description: Public template id from `table_templates action "search"`: company, people, creator, or posts. Omit for a fully custom schema. Use company for company-list, TAM, ICP, prospecting, or Growth sourcing tables; use creator for creator or influencer accounts.

name.description: Display name. Optional when `template` is set (falls back to template label). Required when no template.

description.description: Explicit mode: 1-2 sentence description of what this table stores and why it exists. May be omitted when purpose already supplies that description.

icon.description: Explicit user-requested icon override. Omit when using a template so its suggested Lucide icon is preserved; never invent an emoji. Custom tables otherwise default to 'folder.fill'.

color.description: Hex color code (default from template or '#B87EFE')

schema.description: Schema defining fields and display config. With `template`, `schema.fields` adds or overrides fields on top of the template baseline; omit it when the template already covers the request. Without a template, this is the full schema.

key.description: Field identifier (snake_case)

type.description: Data type. Pick the most specific one: `url` for links/websites/domains, `email`, `phone`, `number`, `date` — don't default everything to `string`. `enum`/`array` are the UI's Select/Multi-select; `boolean` is the Checkbox type. Use `object` for a self-contained bag of attributes. For a timestamp, use `date` with `date_format: 'datetime'`. For a cross-table link, use an `item_ref` field whose `target_database_id` names the target table.

target_database_id.description: For `item_ref` fields: the table whose items this field points at.

label.description: Human-readable label in English (e.g. 'Full Name', 'Job Title'). Defaults to a humanized version of `key` if omitted.

options.description: Allowed values for enum / array type. Either a list of plain strings (preferred, e.g. ['active','passed']) or a list of {value, label?} objects.

description.description: REQUIRED. Brief description of what this field stores and how AI should fill it (e.g. 'The person\'s current job title at their company'). Always provide a meaningful description.

is_unique.description: If true, this field is the unique identifier for deduplication. Exactly ONE field per table MUST have this set to true (e.g. email, linkedin_url, or name).

is_primary.description: Deprecated. Use the table-level `schema.primary_field` instead (omit it and the executor auto-derives from the first field). Kept for back-compat — if set on exactly one field and `primary_field` is not set, the executor uses this field as the primary.

date_format.description: Only when type='date'. 'date' renders 2026-04-21; 'datetime' renders 2026-04-21 11:45 (minute precision, no seconds). Default: datetime.

contact_platform.description: Only for a `url` field holding a LinkedIn or Instagram PROFILE URL: set 'linkedin' or 'instagram' so inbox conversations from that person auto-pair to this row and campaigns can DM them. actions.name: update_chart
actions.description:
Configure a chart-view dashboard on a database. Charts are AI-curated: every panel is one intentional, thoughtfully-chosen card — there is no auto-fan-out and no auto-generated panels. One panel = one card on screen. **Storage**: chart_panels live PER saved view, under `databases.view_configs.saved_views[i].chart_panels`. You MUST pass `savedViewId` so the right view is updated; different chart-type saved views have independent dashboards. **Best chart for ranked momentum**: use `chart_type: 'top_n_per_group'` with `aggregation: 'delta'` or `'growth_rate'` (and `window_days`) to surface fastest-moving entries. Filter to a single platform/category per panel rather than relying on auto-fan-out — one panel for X, another for Reddit, etc. **Empty config**: when a chart-view has no panels, the user sees an empty state. That is the correct default — only create panels the user actually asked for.

show_timeline.description: Show a 'signals over time' line chart at the top of THIS view (default: false). Opt-in only.

Use 'delta' for absolute change, 'growth_rate' for % change (good for surfacing small viral accounts). Default: 'avg' for numbers, 'count' for enums; use 'max' for top-N-per-group with snapshot values.

actions.name: create
actions.description:
Create one or more structured items (rows) in a table — use this to SEED rows with their identity columns (name / company / URL plus the is_unique field), e.g. after finding a list of companies or people. A typed information-tool result is an opaque temporary list: import it through this same operation by passing resultRef instead of data/items. The server maps compatible same-key fields automatically; pass fieldMap only for destination keys that differ, as { destination_table_field: source_result_field }. For a result import, fixedData applies the same schema-keyed values to every imported row, such as one tag or source-post relation. It imports all matching result rows in bounded server batches without refetching or putting them in model context. When the imported cohort fits the normal downstream selection limit, the result also returns an opaque selection that can be passed unchanged to item_query action "list", item_manage action "update", item_manage action "delete", enrichment_run action "run", people_search, or record_manage action "create" with a Sheet source. To FILL an AI-derived attribute (CEO, LinkedIn, email, industry, size…) across rows — especially a multi-step or gated one like 'find the CEO, then the LinkedIn only for the ones with a CEO' — do NOT research each value with web_search/contact-data lookup and write it here; set it up as an Enrich column instead (enrichment_manage action "enable" → enrichment_run action "run"), which gives you the run-if gate, cost-tiering, caching, and a re-runnable column. CRITICAL: each item's data MUST use the exact field keys and value types defined in the table schema. For an item_ref/relation field, write ONLY { database_id: the field's target_database_id, entry_id: the actual target item UUID }; a raw UUID string is rejected. Read or create the target item first so you have its real item id. If the schema has an is_unique field, matching items are updated instead of duplicated. Executes directly.

actions.name: create
actions.description:
Save Records into a Records collection through exactly one source mode. For preserved typed search results pass resultRef and optionally the destination listId; the server resolves identities and retains Record relations without an intermediate Sheet. For one inline Record pass `data`; for several inline Records pass `records` once and never loop. When the Records already exist in a Sheet, pass `source` with its tableId and exactly one scope: an opaque `selection`, already-known `rowIds`, or explicit `all: true`. If that bounded import reports remaining rows, call record_manage action "create" again with the same objectId, runId, and sourceTableId it returned. The server infers deterministic canonical People/Companies mappings and keeps source-row provenance and a resumable import ledger; use mapping overrides only when needed. tools.description: Enable or disable a maintained enrichment column.

actions.name: enable
actions.description:
Turn on Enrich for ONE Sheet column or Records field so the AI can fill that field's cells. Creates a hidden, field-bound workflow: `whatToDo` becomes its instruction (the "What to do"), and the brain fills the field using each row or Record's full context. Creator Fit Score or Fit Reason requires a creator_qualification recipe carrying the user's rubric. Do not configure a Creator score with whatToDo alone. Cross-platform Creator profiles stay in separate platform fields or rows unless the user has already verified they belong together; automatic profile resolution is unavailable. Primary fields cannot be enriched. A missing Records identity such as email or domain may be added through the Record Resolver, but an existing identity is never replaced. For a List, pass listId and its recordDatabaseId to enrich shared Record fields, or its entryDatabaseId for List-owned fields. Shared Record enrichment is manual and limited to explicit active members; verified updates are visible in other Lists. Idempotent per (optional List, container, field): if already on, this just updates the instruction. After enabling, call `enrichment_run action "run"` to actually fill cells.

Rules:
- Requires a Project context: pass projectId.
- recipe.strategy: Email Finder waterfall providers must be unique. LinkedIn Finder waterfall providers must be unique. Phone Finder waterfall providers must be unique.

actions.name: edit_flows
actions.description:
Read workflow_query action "get" first; validate changes together. Enrich uses its saved task, no caller context; maxCredits bounds model/research/provider usage per input across resumes and stops on insufficient/uncertain budget. Add nodes with ref and after; entries are roots. Bind reachable outputs; ['$output'] means whole result. Routes follow declared pass/fail, caseId/default or legacy category schemas. Transform joins require explicit bindings to every unconditional parent; conditional/implicit fan-in is rejected. Wait delays downstream work, preserves prior outputs, has no output. Output owns mapping/write policy; no destination means preview. Preserve File/Tool Access, contextMentions and mappings. Resolve IDs before use; @ stores contextMentions; slash text never activates Skills. Use Listening/Agent for acquisition and Campaign for outreach. Input owns events, webhooks and schedules. actions.name: create
actions.description:
Create one first-class single-channel Campaign owned by the current Project, with one current Message/Wait template. The audience is a Workspace Common Records collection; Sheets are worksheets, and a List uses its backing Records collection plus an opaque Record selection. It never creates a Workflow, adds contacts, prepares, starts, schedules, or sends; use campaign_manage action "manage" with that Records collection selection. Choose one channel per Campaign: Email, LinkedIn, or Instagram. Each Message channel must be exactly email, linkedin_dm, instagram_dm, or linkedin_connect. LinkedIn invitations and DMs share one channel; create separate Campaigns for different channels. A LinkedIn DM sequence starts with a connection invitation and waits for acceptance. Invitation notes require linkedin_premium_confirmed=true for every selected sender from sender_query action "get_settings"; otherwise use includeNote=false only with the user's authorization. Premium uses verified subscription evidence or manual fallback, never connection history. By default each channel uses all eligible connected accounts; pass a sender override only when the user explicitly chose one.

Rules:
- Requires a Project context: pass projectId.
- steps[]: includeNote is only valid for a LinkedIn invitation. Message copy is required. Email subject and thread mode are only valid for Email steps.

actions.name: manage
actions.description:
Manage one Campaign. For people operations use action=people with operation=enroll, return_to_prepare, regenerate, or keep_messages and exactly one target: known campaignRecipientIds (type=ids), or an unchanged selection token (type=selection). To target everyone, first campaign_query action "get" view=selection phase=prepare or sending; this snapshots every matching person across pages. Never clear other people's readiness or use campaign-wide start for a selected set. Regenerate all uses the Prepare selection. Active Campaign content changes, regeneration and keep require explicit Pause first; never automatically pause/resume. A paused Campaign stays paused when people enroll. Legacy singular actions remain compatible. Campaign has one current Message/Wait template: saving it replaces the current template and marks unsent prepared messages for review; it does not generate messages. There is no publish, draft revision, template version, or expectedVersion. Use campaign_query action "get" with the matching view first. Template add_message/update_message accepts sender automatic, specific accountId, or Email-only group groupId from sender_query action "get_settings" sender_groups. Choosing a sender on any Email step updates all Email steps; a new Email with omitted sender inherits that choice. LinkedIn and Instagram sender changes affect only the selected step. Email Messages expose subjectPrompt or exact subject through content plus threadMode; the first Email starts a new thread, later Emails reply by default, and a later new_thread must be explicit. A LinkedIn DM must have an earlier LinkedIn invitation; the first DM after an invite is always acceptance-gated. Invitation notes require linkedin_premium_confirmed=true for every selected sender from sender_query action "get_settings"; unknown or unconfirmed accounts must use includeNote=false. Never infer Premium or silently discard requested notes. Author a note-free invitation as add_message with channel='linkedin_connect', includeNote=false, and no content. Remove a note from an existing invitation with update_message and includeNote=false; content may be omitted or supplied as exact content with an empty body. Adding People accepts a short-lived Records selection token; List selections use the backing Records collection, so raw Record ids stay out of model context. set_person_ready with ready=false returns an enrolled person to preparation, stops unfinished sends and preserves sent history; claimed, dispatching or unconfirmed sends must settle first. Regeneration protects sent, manually edited and in-flight messages. keep_person_messages retains every editable outdated message for one unenrolled person without AI generation, using the current saved copy. Pause the Campaign first. It preserves sent history and stops at the first failed save; inspect the returned kept and remaining message IDs and reconcile unknown outcomes through campaign_query action "get" before retrying. Starting snapshots each prepared message, enrolled contact endpoint, sender, channel, and schedule into durable planned items; it never sends inline.

Rules:
- Requires a Project context: pass projectId.
- changes[]: includeNote is only valid for a LinkedIn invitation. threadMode is only valid for Email messages. Message content is required. A Message update must change at least one field. Empty exact content is only valid when removing a LinkedIn invitation note.

input.title: manage
input.description: Manage one Campaign. For people operations use action=people with operation=enroll, return_to_prepare, regenerate, or keep_messages and exactly one target: known campaignRecipientIds (type=ids), or an unchanged selection token (type=selection). To target everyone, first campaign_query action "get" view=selection phase=prepare or sending; this snapshots every matching person across pages. Never clear other people's readiness or use campaign-wide start for a selected set. Regenerate all uses the Prepare selection. Active Campaign content changes, regeneration and keep require explicit Pause first; never automatically pause/resume. A paused Campaign stays paused when people enroll. Legacy singular actions remain compatible. Campaign has one current Message/Wait template: saving it replaces the current template and marks unsent prepared messages for review; it does not generate messages. There is no publish, draft revision, template version, or expectedVersion. Use campaign_query action "get" with the matching view first. Template add_message/update_message accepts sender automatic, specific accountId, or Email-only group groupId from sender_query action "get_settings" sender_groups. Choosing a sender on any Email step updates all Email steps; a new Email with omitted sender inherits that choice. LinkedIn and Instagram sender changes affect only the selected step. Email Messages expose subjectPrompt or exact subject through content plus threadMode; the first Email starts a new thread, later Emails reply by default, and a later new_thread must be explicit. A LinkedIn DM must have an earlier LinkedIn invitation; the first DM after an invite is always acceptance-gated. Invitation notes require linkedin_premium_confirmed=true for every selected sender from sender_query action "get_settings"; unknown or unconfirmed accounts must use includeNote=false. Never infer Premium or silently discard requested notes. Author a note-free invitation as add_message with channel='linkedin_connect', includeNote=false, and no content. Remove a note from an existing invitation with update_message and includeNote=false; content may be omitted or supplied as exact content with an empty body. Adding People accepts a short-lived Records selection token; List selections use the backing Records collection, so raw Record ids stay out of model context. set_person_ready with ready=false returns an enrolled person to preparation, stops unfinished sends and preserves sent history; claimed, dispatching or unconfirmed sends must settle first. Regeneration protects sent, manually edited and in-flight messages. keep_person_messages retains every editable outdated message for one unenrolled person without AI generation, using the current saved copy. Pause the Campaign first. It preserves sent history and stops at the first failed save; inspect the returned kept and remaining message IDs and reconcile unknown outcomes through campaign_query action "get" before retrying. Starting snapshots each prepared message, enrolled contact endpoint, sender, channel, and schedule into durable planned items; it never sends inline.

Use this instead of authoring a Workflow for external content discovery. Choose exact signal endpoint ids and write their inputs and include/exclude filters. Do not add tags unless the user explicitly asked to classify or tag collected posts; Category and Sentiment are never defaults. Every source is created switched OFF. After the user chooses to enable collection, use listening_manage action "update" for selected free sources or listening_manage action "activate" for paid sources; follow the returned result for approval requirements. If the user wants reply strategies but has not supplied shared voice/context for replyDefaults, ask whether they want to provide it directly or have you inspect a specific social profile and its recent posts/replies through the supported social tools; do not invent the strategy. Conditional reply strategies require the corresponding tags in the same call. Strategies must be mutually exclusive; use no all-posts fallback when some posts should intentionally receive no generated draft. Use listening_query action "get" then listening_manage action "update" for an existing Listening.

- Requires a Project context: pass projectId.

include.description: Complete post-content criteria: what a collected post must discuss, describe, or demonstrate to be kept. For an already-selected account, describe which of its posts the user wants to see, not who to monitor. Source identity/schedule belong in signals; commenter/reactor/reposter capture belongs in Engager rules; downstream outreach and reply goals are not content filters. Do not infer buying intent or invent topical restrictions from those goals. If the user wants every post, set filterMode=bypass and preserve the existing criteria. null clears it; omit to preserve it.

exclude.description: Complete post-content criteria for rejecting posts: only unwanted topics, post types, or meanings specified by the user. filterMode.description: Whether to score posts against Include/Exclude or bypass content scoring and keep every collected post. Omit to preserve the mode. Editing criteria alone never leaves bypass mode, and bypass preserves criteria for later. Tags and Engager rules remain independent.

input.title: update
input.description: Change one existing Listening after reading it with listening_query action "get". Every field is optional and omitted fields stay unchanged. When signals, tags, replyStrategies, or replyDefaults are supplied, each value is the complete desired set: preserve every existing sibling you still want, and pass [] only when the user explicitly wants all strategies removed. Signals are keyed by endpointId, so multiple source types from one platform may coexist. LinkedIn keyword and account sources share a fixed recent 7-day publication window before scoring and saving; account retrieval checks up to 10 posts, not exhaustive coverage. Enabling Engagers does not expand that window. New Signals default OFF unless enabled is explicitly true. Paid sources need listening_manage action "activate" after saving inputs. Reply strategies must be mutually exclusive; do not create a fallback if unmatched posts should keep an empty composer.

actions.name: engage_list
actions.description:
Manage independent Listening Engagers cards, each with its own capture rule, managed Sheet and daily people limit. Use list first, create a new card or update its exact ruleId. New cards use one sheetRoutes item with a new sheetName and exact saved post tagFilters; keep the bound sheetId on updates. Select any nonempty subset of LinkedIn comment, reaction and repost authors with interactionTypes, for Person, Company and Unknown profiles without relevance screening or Records admission. Locked Profile type preserves Person, Company or Unknown classification. Keep genuine headlines and one Source column containing the matched keyword or tracked account. Cards collect and bill independently, including overlapping posts; do not promise shared reads across cards. Existing multi-route rules retain their bindings. Each Sheet locks source/identity fields while allowing custom Enrich, scoring and labels. Guide Sheet configuration separately; this tool never enriches, scores or creates People Records. Import selected Sheet rows into Records before Campaign use. New cards default OFF. Enabling collection needs the exact returned recurring credit approval. Deleting preserves saved Sheet rows, Lists and Records, and removes raw capture history including pending observations.

Rules:
- Requires a Project context when action is create or update or delete or sync: pass projectId.
- sheetRoutes[]: Choose an Engagers Sheet or name a new Sheet for each route.

actions.name: send
actions.description:
Prepare a public reply to one explicitly selected Listening post. accountId is optional: use the account saved with its draft, then the matching strategy or Listening platform default, or the sole ready account; ask the user when several are available without a default. An unavailable saved account must be reconnected or explicitly replaced. The server requires confirmation of the exact target, sender and body before posting. X keyword-discovered posts require copying the draft and replying manually on the original post; a connected X account alone does not permit direct replies. Use the user's chosen draft verbatim. Read the result; failures or uncertain delivery are not success and must not be blindly retried. For several selected posts call separately with each exact postId and body.

actions.name: write
actions.description:
Write a Content post as a draft, targeting one or more connected accounts. Saves without scheduling — the person reviews the per-platform preview and schedules it themselves. Pass `postId` to rewrite an existing draft. Give an account its own `body` only when its copy should differ; otherwise leave it out and the account uses the shared body. In native SignalSurf chat, set `attachFiles` to attach images or video from the message. External agents first transfer their original files with content_manage.upload, then supply completed `mediaUploadIds` in attachment order. When rewriting, omit `mediaUploadIds` to keep each account's saved media, pass [] to remove it, or supply your own completed uploads to replace it. Any authorized Content collaborator can edit the shared draft.

Rules:
- Requires a Project context: pass projectId.

actions.description:
Transfer images/videos from external agents including Grok Bot and OpenAI Dots. Read the user's real file on your cloud computer. Prepare returns a binary HTTP upload request for files up to 100 MB; send exact bytes, then complete the same uploadId. Prepare with bytesBase64 instead transfers a file up to 2 MiB directly through MCP and returns ready. Never invent bytes. Use completed IDs in content_manage action "write". Multiple images keep caller order. Local paths, arbitrary URLs and documents are not accepted as tool inputs. Requires uploadId and operationId for exact retry. If the result is unknown, complete the same uploadId before retrying. Does not publish.

- Requires a Project context: pass projectId.
- Inline MCP files must be at most 2 MiB; use the binary upload request for larger files.

actions.name: search
actions.description: Bot Memory is private execution context, working state and recollections, separate from formal Knowledge; it never stores or edits those documents. Verify recalled company facts/decisions against current Knowledge revisions; never share private User memory automatically. Formal Knowledge is inspectable, versioned Workspace Markdown edited only by AI. knowledge_query search discovers references and Markdown with separate rankings; report partial coverage. Use knowledge_query documents for full files, versions and classification; knowledge_manage document edits. Native project_knowledge_query/manage use pinned Run authority. Editing requires an active Project and selected file. Read before writing; require a confirmed saved version receipt. Explicitly retain failed/inconclusive trials, evidence and decisions; background extraction does not save Knowledge. AI manages folders without manual-placement locks. Uploaded references retain Knowledge Base ownership and separate Base list/save actions. Knowledge stores durable company identity, decisions, hypotheses, evidence, strategy and reusable procedures. Get current connected integrations, accounts, senders, mailboxes, table inventories, open threads, task or trigger status and operational counters from their canonical tools when needed. These live tool-discoverable snapshots do not belong in Knowledge or Profile. A durable policy about using a tool or sender belongs in its own subject; company Profile contains only company identity. When saving Knowledge, search existing documents first. Library categories come from persisted documentType and placement, not free folder names. On create choose documentType and placement atomically. Use classify with metadataVersion to change type or explicitly move home; omit placement to preserve home. Shared Library types are product (Offerings), persona, use_case, segment, competitor, reference_customer and proof. Company identity uses profile; writing guidance uses style. These nine are the fixed shared Library categories and remain visible when empty. angle, strategy, research and other are Project-only types, never shared categories. Legacy Project documents without a surviving Project ID stay under Projects until their origin is verified. reference_customer requires an actual customer reference, not a prospect list. Project strategy, hypotheses, message tests and local research belong to placement project in the active Project; reusable validated business context belongs to placement workspace. Append/correct/rename and attaching/opening a file preserve its existing home and identity. Read the current document before updating; update its original subject rather than copying a shared file into a Project. Never promote local observations to reusable claims without grounded evidence. Distinguish company identity, products, ICPs, personas, message angles, competitors, reply style and evidence when the actual content warrants separate documents. Categories are fixed; never create, rename or nest category folders. Distinguish product-specific documents through category names or document titles and keep Play-specific assumptions in that Project. A reference contact is not a validated persona. Projects start without Knowledge files. Create a document only when useful grounded content needs to be retained; read and update an existing document for the same subject. Empty fixed categories and the Projects section remain visible without creating documents. Projects is a separate section with one flat document group per Project; it is not a custom category. Search team sources by meaning and cite returned source identities. Explicit Base IDs restrict search to references.

input.title: document
input.description: Knowledge stores durable company identity, decisions, hypotheses, evidence, strategy and reusable procedures. Get current connected integrations, accounts, senders, mailboxes, table inventories, open threads, task or trigger status and operational counters from their canonical tools when needed. These live tool-discoverable snapshots do not belong in Knowledge or Profile. A durable policy about using a tool or sender belongs in its own subject; company Profile contains only company identity. When saving Knowledge, search existing documents first. Library categories come from persisted documentType and placement, not free folder names. On create choose documentType and placement atomically. Use classify with metadataVersion to change type or explicitly move home; omit placement to preserve home. Shared Library types are product (Offerings), persona, use_case, segment, competitor, reference_customer and proof. Company identity uses profile; writing guidance uses style. These nine are the fixed shared Library categories and remain visible when empty. angle, strategy, research and other are Project-only types, never shared categories. Legacy Project documents without a surviving Project ID stay under Projects until their origin is verified. reference_customer requires an actual customer reference, not a prospect list. Project strategy, hypotheses, message tests and local research belong to placement project in the active Project; reusable validated business context belongs to placement workspace. Append/correct/rename and attaching/opening a file preserve its existing home and identity. Read the current document before updating; update its original subject rather than copying a shared file into a Project. Never promote local observations to reusable claims without grounded evidence. Distinguish company identity, products, ICPs, personas, message angles, competitors, reply style and evidence when the actual content warrants separate documents. Categories are fixed; never create, rename or nest category folders. Distinguish product-specific documents through category names or document titles and keep Play-specific assumptions in that Project. A reference contact is not a validated persona. Projects start without Knowledge files. Create a document only when useful grounded content needs to be retained; read and update an existing document for the same subject. Empty fixed categories and the Projects section remain visible without creating documents. Projects is a separate section with one flat document group per Project; it is not a custom category. Explicitly write complete Markdown. Read full text and classification policy first. Append preserves context; correct replaces one unique exact passage; rename preserves identity. Retry unknown outcomes with the original tool identity; reread conflicts. Forget only on an explicit named request; never infer deletion or invent results. Editing requires an active Project with the file selected. Attach/detach changes selection without copying Markdown. Use classify/link/unlink and related reads to preserve relationships. Native body writes require pinned human evidence. Claim success only after a confirmed saved receipt.

actions.name: update_settings
actions.description:
Update one connected sender account. Email supports signature, open tracking, unsubscribe link, sending window, daily send cap, and warm-up. LinkedIn supports weekly invitation/message quotas. Instagram supports its daily DM cap; keep dailyLimit ≤ 50. Incompatible fields are never persisted, and the result reports every requested field as applied, unsupported, or failed. Read sender_query action "get_settings" first when the account and current values are not already in conversation context.

Rules:
- Change synthetic warm-up separately from sender settings.
- At least one sender setting is required.
- syntheticWarmup.settings: Recommended mode uses the provider ceiling; custom mode requires a ceiling. Minimum warm-up emails cannot exceed the maximum.
- sendingWindow: End must be after start.

syntheticWarmup.description: Manage purchased email warming for this exact account. actions.name: upsert
actions.description:
Automatically save or update durable facts, preferences, profiles or maintained topics grounded in the user's conversation for the explicit authorized User, Workspace or Project audience. Do not ask for per-item save confirmation. Read the current block first and supply its exact version plus complete replacement details preserving unrelated facts. Use null baseVersion only for a new ordinary subject or with the exact profileToken for Workspace Profile. Do not store private transcripts, temporary requests, unconfirmed outcomes, credentials, or inferred sensitive personal facts. Returns a canonical Memory receipt available across clients. If a subject was forgotten, recreate it only after the user explicitly asks to remember it again, using fresh user-provided contents.

Rules:
- Project Memory uses named Topic or Area blocks.
- Workspace Profile requires its opaque token and null baseVersion; other Memory uses integer versions.
- A Project selector is only valid for Project Memory.

actions.name: write
actions.description: Knowledge stores durable company identity, decisions, hypotheses, evidence, strategy and reusable procedures. Get current connected integrations, accounts, senders, mailboxes, table inventories, open threads, task or trigger status and operational counters from their canonical tools when needed. These live tool-discoverable snapshots do not belong in Knowledge or Profile. A durable policy about using a tool or sender belongs in its own subject; company Profile contains only company identity. When saving Knowledge, search existing documents first. Library categories come from persisted documentType and placement, not free folder names. On create choose documentType and placement atomically. Use classify with metadataVersion to change type or explicitly move home; omit placement to preserve home. Shared Library types are product (Offerings), persona, use_case, segment, competitor, reference_customer and proof. Company identity uses profile; writing guidance uses style. These nine are the fixed shared Library categories and remain visible when empty. angle, strategy, research and other are Project-only types, never shared categories. Legacy Project documents without a surviving Project ID stay under Projects until their origin is verified. reference_customer requires an actual customer reference, not a prospect list. Project strategy, hypotheses, message tests and local research belong to placement project in the active Project; reusable validated business context belongs to placement workspace. Append/correct/rename and attaching/opening a file preserve its existing home and identity. Read the current document before updating; update its original subject rather than copying a shared file into a Project. Never promote local observations to reusable claims without grounded evidence. Distinguish company identity, products, ICPs, personas, message angles, competitors, reply style and evidence when the actual content warrants separate documents. Categories are fixed; never create, rename or nest category folders. Distinguish product-specific documents through category names or document titles and keep Play-specific assumptions in that Project. A reference contact is not a validated persona. Projects start without Knowledge files. Create a document only when useful grounded content needs to be retained; read and update an existing document for the same subject. Empty fixed categories and the Projects section remain visible without creating documents. Projects is a separate section with one flat document group per Project; it is not a custom category. Explicitly write complete Markdown. Read full text and classification policy first. Append preserves context; correct replaces one unique exact passage; rename preserves identity. Retry unknown outcomes with the original tool identity; reread conflicts. Forget only on an explicit named request; never infer deletion or invent results. Editing requires an active Project with the file selected. Attach/detach changes selection without copying Markdown. Use classify/link/unlink and related reads to preserve relationships. Native body writes require pinned human evidence. Claim success only after a confirmed saved receipt.
